about: What the index must make of the synthetic corpus of Worker/tests/dicom_factory.py (ADR 0026 decision 1), derived by hand from ADRs 0022 to 0024. Series are named by scenario and description, never by UID. corpus_check.compare holds a merged project.sqlite to it.

review.gate: A regression test until the owner has reviewed this file; then M2's acceptance gate (ADR 0026 decision 2).

job.selection: the defaults of ADR 0023 decision 8, as Protocol/fixtures/jobs/index_scan.json writes them
job.identity: the defaults of ADR 0024: the placeholder list, folder_ids true, folder_max_level 3

features.permissions: A file and a folder with mode 000 are written only where a probe shows the mode is enforced (not as root).
features.non_utf8_names: A file name with the byte 0xE9 is written only where the file system accepts it (not APFS).

conventions.rule: check.too_few_slices is raised on every image part, DICOM or NIfTI, of any modality, whose slice_count is known and below min_slices; select.excluded.too_few_slices likewise needs a known slice_count.
conventions.why: The registry lists the check, and ADR 0023 the exclusion, without saying where either applies.

conventions.rule: Geometry checks (no_geometry, gap, uneven_spacing, duplicate_positions, gantry_tilt, tilt_tag_only, oblique) are raised on image parts only, a Secondary Capture included.
conventions.why: ADR 0022 decision 11 computes geometry per part; a dose report has none to report.

conventions.rule: A missing ImageType gives select.excluded.image_type_missing alone.
conventions.why: The conditions on value 0 and on the plane say nothing more about an ImageType that is not there.

conventions.rule: image_type_value names the first excluded value in ImageType order; description names the first configured term that matches.
conventions.why: A reason holds one params object, so one value and one term.

conventions.rule: A NIfTI part skips the ImageType conditions; a NULL description matches no term.
conventions.why: A NIfTI file has no ImageType; ADR 0022 decision 13 lets its name stand in.

conventions.rule: A held part keeps the worker's rank (auto_rank 1, auto_selected 1) with selected 0 and is_primary 0, and its reason is outcome held with select.held.unconfirmed_patient alone; the worker's reason waits in if_confirmed, which compare does not read.
conventions.why: ADR 0023's eligibility table has the merge apply select.held.unconfirmed_patient, and ADR 0029 makes IndexSQL.merge write it; the confirmation or assignment that releases the study gives the worker's reason back.

conventions.rule: check.duplicates counts every file that lost its instance, the loser of a UID conflict included; check.uid_conflict counts the losers whose study or series UID differs from the winner's, on the winner's part; check.uid_conflict_lost counts the same losers on the part of their own series. A series whose only file lost has no part, so the corpus's stray file shows only on the winner's side; test_index_group.py holds the loser's side.
conventions.why: ADR 0022 decision 8 counts losers in duplicates and uses the winner's grouping; ADR 0029 adds the loser's side, whose series otherwise lost files without a word.

conventions.rule: truncated, missing pixel data and transfer syntax are judged on winning files only.
conventions.why: The losers are not what the converter reads.

conventions.rule: Parts of a split series are told apart by what differs (modality, orientation, matrix, spacing); part is asserted only where ADR 0022's numbering decides it (same lowest position, then the lower InstanceNumber).
conventions.why: The ADR orders parts by position along each part's own normal, which says nothing for a part without positions.

conventions.rule: A NIfTI study has no date, description or age; its patient's accession_numbers is an empty JSON array.
conventions.why: A NIfTI header carries none of them; the merge writes json_group_array of nothing.

conventions.rule: An unnamed NIfTI file has pid_state missing and folder candidates (levels 0 and 1, "nifti"), so its patient is unconfirmed, one per file.
conventions.why: ADR 0024 decision 3 records candidates for every study whose PatientID is missing.

conventions.rule: Enhanced CT takes thickness, rescale and kernel from the functional groups, so its volume has no check.no_rescale; a part with a file of mixed frames has no geometry: no slice count, extent, spacing or orientation, check.no_geometry beside check.enhanced_mixed_frames, and excluded by no_geometry and mixed_frames.
conventions.why: ADR 0022 decision 3 reads the functional groups a second time; ADR 0028 decision 3 decides that a part with a file of mixed frames has no geometry.

conventions.rule: check.pet_not_attenuation_corrected is raised when CorrectedImage is present without ATTN, not when it is absent.
conventions.why: ADR 0022 decision 12 stores NULL for an absent tag, which says nothing is known.

conventions.rule: A Part 10 file cut inside its file meta, and one whose DICM is followed by no dataset, are unreadable with read.invalid_dicom.
conventions.why: pydicom raises on the first and returns an empty dataset, without SOP UIDs, for the second.

conventions.rule: A .nii or .nii.gz without a valid NIfTI-1 header is an archive when it is gzip and not_dicom otherwise.
conventions.why: ADR 0022 decision 2's table.

conventions.rule: check.sex_conflict's values are compared as a set.
conventions.why: group_concat(DISTINCT …) has no defined order.

conventions.rule: identifiers.patient_id is the normalized PatientID (stripped, NFC), the study's most frequent one.
conventions.why: ADR 0024 decision 1 normalizes before linking; the pending identifier is assumed to be what was linked.

conventions.rule: study_date is ISO 8601 (YYYY-MM-DD).
conventions.why: IndexSQL.patientAges computes julianday(study_date), which reads no other form.

conventions.rule: Numbers compare to within 0.001; ages in days and weeks use 365.2425 and 52.1775 per year (pseudonym.parse_dicom_age).
conventions.why: Lengths and angles are stored as computed; parameters are rounded to 0.001.

conventions.rule: A source's checks have object_key = its source_id as text.
conventions.why: IndexSQL.merge copies cat_checks.object_ref for sources.

checks.why: junk/README.txt, empty.dat, random.bin, report.pdf, short.dcm (100 bytes), raw_dataset.dcm (no preamble) and nifti/garbage.nii. .DS_Store, Thumbs.db, desktop.ini, ._IM0001.dcm and the files in .Spotlight-V100, .Trashes, .fseventsd, .TemporaryItems and .DocumentRevisions-V100 are skipped without a row.
export.zip, series.tar, notes.txt.gz, backup.7z, backup.rar, and nifti/broken.nii.gz, a gzip that is no NIfTI (C15).
junk/cut_meta.dcm, cut inside its file meta, and junk/dicm_garbage.dcm, the preamble and DICM followed by no dataset (C14).

catalog.why: Image files by folder: selection 999 (thin_thick 153, coverage 112, kernel 200, kernel_not_sharp, warnings, series_number, tie and multiphase 100 each, description 15, image_type 19), splits 76, geometry 84, pixels 150, syntaxes 42, duplicates 116, enhanced 4, petct 130, identity 33, anonymous 62, canary 3, kernels 30, dicomdir 8, nfd 3; 1 740. Non-image: the dose report and the split SR. Truncated: two in pixels and the losing copy in duplicates/copy_a; missing: one. A deflated file's pixel state is not asserted.

scenarios.name: selection.thin_thick
scenarios.covers: A localizer, a 1 mm and a 2 mm series over the same 100 mm, a dose report, and an AppleDouble file beside a slice. The thinner of two equal coverages wins.

parts.why: ORIGINAL\PRIMARY\LOCALIZER: LOCALIZER is an excluded value and no value from 2 on is AXIAL. The coronal normal (0, 1, 0) has n_z = 0. One position: no spacing, so no thickness to fall back to. T20s is in no kernel list.
Both series cover 0 to 100 mm (100.0 each), so coverage ties; 1.0 mm is more than 0.02 mm thinner than 2.0 mm.
An X-Ray Radiation Dose SR: every failing condition is listed. A non-image part gets no geometry checks (C2) and, without a slice count, no too_few_slices (C1).

scenarios.name: selection.coverage
scenarios.covers: A 300 mm abdomen against a thinner 100 mm liver series: coverage decides before thickness. The abdomen numbers every slice as its own acquisition, which is no reason to split because no position repeats.

parts.why: 61 slices from -300 to 0 mm in 5 mm steps: 300 mm. The liver covers -150 to -50 mm, 100 mm, which is below 300 - 1.0.

scenarios.name: selection.kernel
scenarios.covers: Four equal series that differ in kernel only: soft, unknown, missing and sharp.

parts.why: All four cover 0 to 147 mm at 3 mm. Br40d is Siemens br40 plus the suffix d: soft, and the only soft one, so it wins at step 3.
bv38 is in no list (bv36 and bv40 are soft): unknown. Rank 2 over the missing kernel, which is unknown too, by series number 4 < 5. Every eligible reason names the step of the first cascade: kernel.
Br64d is Siemens br64 plus d: sharp, so last although its series number is the lowest.

scenarios.name: selection.kernel_not_sharp
scenarios.covers: An unknown kernel against a sharp one: it wins, and the reason must not call it soft.

scenarios.name: selection.warnings
scenarios.covers: Two equal series, one without rescale slope and intercept: the warning decides.

parts.why: B30f is Siemens b30 plus f: soft, like A's. Coverage, thickness, kernel and ImageType tie; A has one warning-level check, B none.

scenarios.name: selection.series_number
scenarios.covers: Two equal series: the lower series number decides, whatever the folder order.

scenarios.name: selection.tie
scenarios.covers: Two series equal in everything, series number included: the series UID decides.

parts.why: I30f is Siemens i30 plus f: soft. Both are number 8. B's series UID sorts first as a string; test_corpus.py holds that fact of the generator.

scenarios.name: selection.multiphase
scenarios.covers: One series UID holding two phases at the same 50 positions, told apart by AcquisitionNumber: split at step e, and the parts tie up to the part number.

parts.why: Both parts start at z = 0; part 0 is the one with the lower InstanceNumbers (1-50, acquisition 1). Equal in everything else, and they share the series UID, so step 8 decides.

scenarios.name: selection.description
scenarios.covers: Description terms: short terms match whole tokens only (MPR, MIP, 3D), so "Compressed" passes; "Cor" is no term (ADR 0023). Three slices each, so every part is also too short and the study has nothing eligible.

parts.why: "compressed" contains m-p-r, but mpr has three letters and matches whole tokens only.
cor is not a default term: an axial series named for the heart stays eligible (ADR 0023, rejected alternatives).

scenarios.name: selection.image_type
scenarios.covers: The ImageType rule: missing, an unknown value 0, two values, VOLUME in a classic CT, DERIVED\PRIMARY\REFORMATTED, DERIVED\SECONDARY\AXIAL and a Secondary Capture screen save.

parts.why: VOLUME stands in for AXIAL only in Enhanced and Legacy Converted CT, so Classic Volume fails the plane rule; Reformatted fails three conditions.

A Secondary Capture is an image storage class, so not not_image. SECONDARY (value 1) is the first excluded value in ImageType order, before SCREEN SAVE (C4). No orientation or position: no geometry (C2).

scenarios.name: splits
scenarios.covers: Every split reason of ADR 0022 decision 9 that a classic series can have (SOP class, orientation, matrix, pixel spacing, acquisition, phase, echo), and the near misses that must not split.

parts.why: Four CT slices and a Comprehensive SR under one series UID: step a. Which part is 0 is not asserted, since the SR has no position to sort by (C9).
Four axial and four coronal slices: the normals differ by 90°, step b.
16 x 16 and 20 x 20 at the same positions: step c.
0.75 / 0.7 = 1.071, more than 1 % apart: step d.
0.704 / 0.7 = 1.0057, within 1 %: one part. Its pixel spacing is either value and is not asserted.
The same four positions twice; the tag that differs separates the repeats: step e, reason acquisition (acquisition, phase or echo). Part 0 holds the lower InstanceNumbers.
The same four positions twice; the tag that differs separates the repeats: step e, reason acquisition (acquisition, phase or echo). Part 0 holds the lower InstanceNumbers.
The same four positions twice; the tag that differs separates the repeats: step e, reason acquisition (acquisition, phase or echo). Part 0 holds the lower InstanceNumbers.
AcquisitionNumber 1 to 8, but no position repeats: step e does not apply.
z = 0, 3, 6, 9, 9, 12, 15, 18: eight instances, seven distinct positions; the two at 9 share one. Nothing separates them, so the series is not split.

scenarios.name: geometry
scenarios.covers: The geometry checks of ADR 0022 decision 11, one per series: gap, uneven spacing, gantry tilt with shear, a tilt tag without shear, oblique planes on both sides of 18.2°, coronal, sagittal, invalid orientation, missing positions, non-square pixels, varying rescale, a missing kernel and burned-in text.

parts.why: z = 0, 1, 2, 6, 7, 8: steps 1, 1, 4, 1, 1, median 1. 4 > 1.5 is one gap with floor(4 / 1 + 0.5) - 1 = 3 slices missing; the other steps equal the median. No SliceThickness: the thickness falls back to the spacing.
z = 0, 1, 2, 3.25, 4.25, 5.25: steps 1, 1, 1.25, 1, 1. 1.25 is no gap (not above 1.5) and differs from the median by 0.25 > max(0.01, 0.01 mm).

Columns turned 15° about x: n = (0, sin 15°, cos 15°), still axial (0.966). The table moves along z, so the positions advance 3 cos 15° = 2.898 mm along n, 14.489 mm in all, and the line through them is 15° from n: a shear, so gantry_tilt and not tilt_tag_only. The plane is 15° from axial: oblique.
GantryDetectorTilt 12 on an upright stack: no shear.
Normal 10° from z, positions along the normal: no shear, axial (cos 10° = 0.985), so only its length excludes it.
cos 25° = 0.906 < 0.95 and sin 25° = 0.423: no standard plane.
The column cosine (0, 0, 0) has length 0: invalid, so no geometry and no slice count (C1).
PixelSpacing 0.7 \ 0.8: 0.1 > 0.01 x 0.7. pixel_spacing_mm is the row spacing.

scenarios.name: pixel_data
scenarios.covers: Pixel data checked without reading pixels (ADR 0022 decision 4): a native file cut inside its pixel data, an encapsulated file without its Sequence Delimitation Item, and a file without a pixel element.

parts.why: Slice 25 lost its last 256 bytes; its header still reads, so it keeps its position and the part has 50 slices.

scenarios.name: transfer_syntaxes
scenarios.covers: Every transfer syntax pydicom 3.0.2 and imagecodecs 2026.8.16 can write here, three slices each, and a private syntax.

parts.why: The pinned dcm2niix refuses Deflated and JPEG Extended 12-bit and converts the other twelve syntaxes here (ADR 0023 decision 5); an unknown syntax counts as unreadable.
A 2.25 UID made from the seed ("private-syntax"); test_corpus.py holds this value to the generator.

scenarios.name: duplicates
scenarios.covers: One study across two sources: a series copied into a second folder with one truncated copy, a stray file reusing an instance UID under another series, the same instances Deflated and Explicit, and a series present in both sources.

parts.why: 100 files for 50 instances: copy_a wins by path except slice 7, whose copy_a file is truncated, so copy_b's complete copy wins. The stray file has slice 12's SOP UID under another series UID; copy_a wins by path, the stray loses (51 losers, C7) and the instance stays here. Only winners count, so nothing is truncated (C8) and the part is the study's only candidate.
The Deflated copies sort first (a_deflated) but the converter cannot read them, so all five Explicit copies win and the part has no transfer_syntax exclusion.
The same five files in source 1 and source 2: the lower source wins.

studies.why: "Stray Conflict" is not a part: its only file lost its instance to Dup Folders.

scenarios.name: enhanced
scenarios.covers: Enhanced CT: a 50-frame volume with ImageType ORIGINAL\PRIMARY\VOLUME, two files of one series with StackID 1 and 2, and a file whose frames mix axial and coronal.

parts.why: Each frame is an instance (image_count 50). VOLUME passes the plane rule for Enhanced CT. Thickness and rescale come from the functional groups, so no check.no_rescale (C12).
Two files at the same five positions; no acquisition tag separates them, StackID does: step f. A file is never split, so each part is one file; part 0 is the file with InstanceNumber 1.
50 axial and 2 coronal frames in one file, which is never split. ADR 0028 decision 3: such a part has no geometry, so nothing of it is measured, and both codes exclude it (C12).

scenarios.name: pet_ct
scenarios.covers: A PET/CT study: Siemens' low-dose CT (DERIVED\CT_SOM5 SPI\PRIMARY\AXIAL), an original CT, PET with and without attenuation correction and without CorrectedImage, a PET in another Frame of Reference without dose, weight or decay correction, and a PET that does not overlap the CT.

parts.why: Value 0 is DERIVED and accept_derived_primary is off (OPEN_QUESTIONS #24).
ImageType ORIGINAL\PRIMARY has no plane value. 6 slices from -240 to -40 mm in 40 mm steps: 200 mm.
Without CorrectedImage nothing is known about the correction: the pair holds NULL and no check is raised (C13).
z = 100 to 150 mm against the CT's -245 to 0 mm: no overlap, no pair.

scenarios.name: identity
scenarios.covers: One PatientID written NFC and, with a leading space, NFD; PatientAge against the birth date; a birth on 29 February; ages in days, weeks and months; a study whose files carry two PatientIDs; and one with two issuers.

patients.why: " PAT-E\u0301" "01" stripped and NFC is "PAT-\u00c901": one link, one patient. F and M disagree, so sex stays empty. 60 years in 2021 and 50 in 2023 imply births 12 years apart (> 1.5). Nothing is selected, so the age is the first dated study's.

studies.why: PatientAge 060Y; born 1966-08-15, so 57 completed years on 2024-06-01: 3 > 1 apart. PatientAge wins.
Born 1964-02-29: on 2023-02-28 the 59th birthday (1 March in a common year) has not come, so 58.

patients.why: Implied births 2024-06-01 - 60 x 365.2425 d and 2023-02-28 - 58 x 365.2425 d are 271 days apart: no age_inconsistent. The first dated study is the leap day's, 58.

studies.why: 021D = 21 / 365.2425 years; sex U is no sex.
Four files say CONF-A1 and two CONF-B2: the study takes the most frequent link. CONF-B2 gets no patient of its own.

scenarios.name: anonymous
scenarios.covers: Anonymized studies directly below the source root: ANONYMOUS twice in one case folder, an empty PatientID, a lower-case placeholder and no PatientID element. Each is a patient of its own until the user confirms a folder level.

parts.why: Eligible and ranked first by the worker (select.chosen.only_candidate); the merge deselects it because the patient is unconfirmed, and its reason says held (C6).

patients.why: ANONYMOUS is a placeholder: no link, folder candidates at levels 0-3, so unconfirmed. Without a link, 017 A and 017 B are two patients until confirmed. No identifiers row for an unconfirmed patient.

scenarios.name: canary
scenarios.covers: The canary values of ADR 0024. Only identifiers may hold the ID and accession number; the name and birth date are stored nowhere (test_index_privacy.py searches for them).

studies.why: No PatientAge; born 1901-01-01, 123 completed years on 2024-01-15.

scenarios.name: kernels
scenarios.covers: Kernel classes per vendor (ADR 0023 decision 7), asserted through series.kernel_class because three slices keep every part out of the ranking.

parts.why: GE's own soft list. The GE series carry GE-like private groups.
BODY is a body part, no longer in GE's soft list (ADR 0023).
Philips codes match exactly: b is soft and never matches BONE.
Philips takes no suffix letter, so SMOOTHD is not smooth; no other list has it.
TOSHIBA is Canon.
An unknown vendor: every sharp list, then every soft list; Siemens b30 plus f.

scenarios.name: dicomdir
scenarios.covers: A complete DICOMDIR, and one whose copy lost two of the five files it lists.

parts.why: Instances 2 and 4 (z = 3 and 9) are gone; z = 0, 6, 12 remain, evenly spaced, so only the DICOMDIR can tell that anything is missing.

scenarios.name: names
scenarios.covers: File and folder names in NFD (Gefa\u0308\u00dfe, Scha\u0308del), and, where the file system allows it, a file name that is not UTF-8.

scenarios.name: nifti
scenarios.covers: NIfTI files named CT_<id> and PT_<id>, a 4D file, an upper-case extension, files outside the naming convention (one a label mask), a gzip that is no NIfTI and a .nii of noise.

parts.why: 16 x 16 x 60 at 2.5 mm: 59 x 2.5 = 147.5 mm. No SliceThickness, so the spacing stands in. A NIfTI file skips the ImageType rule (C5) and is its own study, without date or description (C10).
PT_N001 joins CT_N001's patient through the same ID. 30 slices at 4 mm: 116 mm. PET checks on a NIfTI file without PET metadata are not decided, so only too_few_slices is asserted.

patients.why: One patient, two studies: each NIfTI file is a study. No age, no sex.

parts.why: 18 x 18 x 60 x 2: not a single 3D volume. Whether a 4D file has geometry is not decided, so only nifti_not_3d is asserted.
CT_N003.NII.GZ: the extension matches without regard to case.
ct_lower: the CT_ prefix is case-sensitive, so modality OT.

patients.why: No ID from a name: pid_state missing, folder candidates, unconfirmed (C11).

parts.why: seg_mask: a label mask beside a CT is never chosen as one.

pairs.why: Same study and Frame of Reference; PET -240 to -40 mm inside the CT's -245 to 0 mm, so the overlap is the PET's 200 mm. Every PT part pairs with every CT part, the excluded low-dose CT included.

accept_derived_primary.why: OPEN_QUESTIONS #24: with the setting on, DERIVED passes when PRIMARY is among values 1 and later.

parts.why: Coverage 245 mm, thickness 5 mm and soft kernels tie; ORIGINAL wins at step 4.
PRIMARY is value 1, so DERIVED passes; REFORMATTED and the missing plane still exclude it. Secondary Axial and the screen save have no PRIMARY and keep derived.
